Town Ward 3 is generally bounded by Parkhill Road to the north, the Otonabee River to the east, Lansdowne Street and Monaghan Road to the south and Medical Drive to the west, and covers approximately 571 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include the CPKC rail line (Havelock Subdivision), Little Lake Cemetery and industrial lands (approximately 8% of the community area). Along or just beyond its edges are St. Peter's Cemetery. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Town Ward 3 includes Millennium Park, Del Crary Park and King Edward Park, and Jackson Creek runs through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 4 schools and the Peterborough Public Library. Trent University - Catharine Parr Traill College is also located in the community. Other notable landmarks include Downtown Peterborough, Little Lake and Peterborough Armoury.

12.04.0054.t:
Monaghan Ward 2, Peterborough

Monaghan Ward covers the west end of Peterborough and takes its name from the former North Monaghan Township, which surrounded the city on the west. Peterborough itself was founded in 1825 with the Peter Robinson Irish settlers and became a city in 1905. Most of the city's annexations of township land came after the Second World War, and residential growth moved north and west from the 1960s. The Peterborough Regional Health Centre opened in this part of the city in 2008.

Monaghan Ward 2 is generally bounded by the Selwyn boundary and Lily Lake Road to the north, Medical Drive to the east, Sherbrooke Street and Lansdowne Street to the south and the Cavan Monaghan boundary to the west, and covers approximately 1,066 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include a quarry or aggregate pit. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Monaghan Ward 2 includes Roper Park, Kawartha Heights Park and Cedargrove Park, and Jackson Creek runs through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 5 schools. Peterborough Regional Health Centre is also located in the community.

12.04.0055.t:
Ashburnham Ward 4, Peterborough

Ashburnham Ward covers the east side of Peterborough, across the Otonabee River from downtown, often called East City. It takes its name from the former Village of Ashburnham, which grew up on the east bank of the river in the 19th century. Ashburnham was annexed by Peterborough in 1904, the same year the Peterborough Lift Lock was completed on the Trent-Severn Waterway. Its older streets near the river were built up in the late 1800s and early 1900s, with later suburban growth further east.

Ashburnham Ward 4 is generally bounded by Douro Ninth Line and Trent–Severn Waterway to the north, Television Road to the east and the Otonabee River and the Otonabee-South Monaghan boundary to the south, and covers approximately 2,272 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include a hydro transmission corridor, the CPKC rail line (Havelock Subdivision), Highway 7, the City Of Peterborough Wastewater Treatment Plant, a hydro transformer station (Otonabee TS) and industrial lands (approximately 5% of the community area). Along or just beyond its edges are Little Lake Cemetery. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Ashburnham Ward 4 includes Trent University Wildlife Sanctuary, Ashburnham Memorial Park and Beavermead Park, and the Trent Canal, the Otonabee River and Trent–Severn Waterway run through or along the community. Peterborough Golf & Country Club and Liftlock Golf Club are located in the area. Residents are served by approximately 7 schools. Trent University is also located in the community. Other notable landmarks include Canadian Canoe Museum.

06.03.0050.t:
Georgetown, Halton Hills

Georgetown grew around mills built by George Kennedy, who settled on the Credit River in 1821. The Grand Trunk Railway arrived in 1856, and Georgetown became a village in 1864 and a town in 1922. Post-war subdivisions such as Delrex (1950s) and Moore Park (1962) were followed by Georgetown South from 1989. Georgetown became part of the Town of Halton Hills in 1974.

Georgetown is generally bounded by Trafalgar Road to the north, the Credit River to the east and Eighth Line and 10 Side Road to the south, and covers approximately 1,903 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include the CN rail line (Halton Subdivision), the CN rail line (Metrolinx Guelph Subdivision), the Metrolinx (GO Transit) rail line, the Georgetown Wastewater Treatment Plant, Greenwood Cemetery and industrial lands (approximately 6% of the community area). Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Georgetown includes Gellert Community Park, Cedarvale Park and Dominion Gardens Park, and Silver Creek and the Credit River run through or along the community. The Club at North Halton is located in the area. Residents are served by approximately 17 schools and the Georgetown branch of the Halton Hills Public Library, and transit is provided by the Georgetown GO Station. Shopping is available at Georgetown Market Place. Georgetown Hospital is also located in the community.

02.07.0060.t:
Exhibition Park, Guelph

Exhibition Park takes its name from the park at its centre, Guelph's oldest park, which was first used for agricultural exhibitions. The neighbourhood grew as the town expanded north past London Road, the former city boundary. Guelph itself was founded in 1827 by John Galt of the Canada Company and became a city in 1879.

Exhibition Park is generally bounded by Speedvale Avenue to the north, the Speed River to the east, London Road to the south and Edinburgh Road to the west, and covers approximately 183 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include the Goderich Subdivision rail line and a cemetery. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Exhibition Park includes Exhibition Park, Herb Markle Park and CNR Spurline Park, and the Speed River runs through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 2 schools. St. Joseph's Health Centre Guelph is also located in the community.

02.07.0280.t:
General Hospital, Guelph

This area is named after Guelph General Hospital, which lies within it in the city's established east-central area. Guelph was founded in 1827 by John Galt of the Canada Company and became a city in 1879. The area is mainly older and mid-20th century housing around the hospital.

General Hospital is generally bounded by Speedvale Avenue to the north, Eramosa Road to the south and the Speed River to the west, and covers approximately 179 hectares.

There are no major adverse influences within the community itself, but the Goderich Subdivision rail line lie along or just beyond its edges. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in General Hospital includes Skov Park, Bullfrog Pond Park and Joseph Wolfond Park East, and the Speed River runs through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 2 schools and the Bullfrog Mall branch of the Guelph Public Library. Homewood Health Centre and Guelph General Hospital are also located in the community.

02.07.0330.t:
Riverside Park, Guelph

This area in north Guelph takes its name from Riverside Park, which opened in 1905 on the Speed River near Woolwich Street. The park began as a stop on the Guelph Radial Railway, and its name was chosen in a contest. The land had been a private farm known as the Lace Farm. The surrounding residential area was built up mainly through the 20th century.

Riverside Park is generally bounded by the Guelph/Eramosa boundary to the north, Woodlawn Road and Victoria Road to the east, Speedvale Avenue to the south and Edinburgh Road and a hydro corridor to the west, and covers approximately 374 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include the Goderich Subdivision rail line, Woodlawn Memorial Park (cemetery) and industrial lands (approximately 7% of the community area). Along or just beyond its edges are a hydro transmission corridor and a hydro transformer station (Campbell Transformer Station (Guelph)). Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Riverside Park includes Riverside Park, Bailey Park and Waverley Drive Park, and the Speed River runs through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 3 schools.

04.12.0010.t:
Alliston, New Tecumseth

Alliston grew around a grist mill built by the Fletcher family on the Boyne River in 1853. The name was adopted in approximately 1856 and is thought to come from Allerston in North Yorkshire, William Fletcher's birthplace. It was incorporated as a village in 1874 and a town in 1891. Growth increased after Honda opened its first plant near the town in 1986, and Alliston became part of the Town of New Tecumseth in 1991.

Alliston is generally bounded by Shephard Avenue to the north and the Adjala-Tosorontio boundary to the west, with its remaining edges following local streets, lot lines or natural features. It covers approximately 1,203 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include the CPKC rail line (MacTier Subdivision), a landfill site, a wastewater treatment plant, Honda of Canada Manufacturing (industrial plant), a cemetery and industrial lands (approximately 17% of the community area). Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Alliston includes Riverdale Park, GA Wright Athletic Field and Deanne Cynthia Rose Park, and the Boyne River runs through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 6 schools and the Main branch of the New Tecumseth Public Library. Stevenson Memorial Hospital is also located in the community.

04.10.0020.t:
Baxter, Essa

Baxter is a small rural community in the Township of Essa, Simcoe County. Essa Township was incorporated in 1850 and was settled mainly as a farming area. In 1991 the township merged with the Thornton Police Village to form the current Township of Essa. Baxter remains one of the township's main rural communities.

Baxter is generally bounded by Denney Drive to the north and the CPKC rail line (MacTier Subdivision) and Murphy Road to the west, with its remaining edges following local streets, lot lines or natural features. It covers approximately 67 hectares.

There are no major adverse influences within the community itself, but the CPKC rail line (MacTier Subdivision) lie along or just beyond its edges. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Residents are served by one school.

04.10.0030.t:
Rural Essa, Essa

This is the rural part of the Township of Essa in Simcoe County. The township was incorporated in 1850 and was settled mainly for farming and lumbering. In 1991 Essa merged with the Thornton Police Village to form the current township. The area includes farmland and small hamlets, and Frederick Banting, co-discoverer of insulin, was born in Essa.

Rural Essa is generally bounded by County Road 90 to the north, County Road 27 to the east, Highway 89 to the south and the Adjala-Tosorontio boundary and County Road 15 to the west, and covers approximately 26,993 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include a hydro transmission corridor, the CPKC rail line (MacTier Subdivision), the Meaford Subdivision rail line, a quarry or aggregate pit, a hydro transformer station, a landfill site, Cookstown United Church Cemetery and Nicholston Cemetery. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Rural Essa includes Worthington Park, and the Nottawasaga River, the Pine River and Bear Creek run through or along the community. Tangle Creek Golf & Country Club and Bear Creek are located in the area. Residents are served by approximately 3 schools and the Base Borden Military and Public Library. Other notable landmarks include Borden Military Museum.

04.11.0040.t:
Lisle, Adjala-Tosorontio

Lisle is a small village in the former Tosorontio Township in Simcoe County. The area was settled as farmland in the 19th century. Adjala Township was incorporated in 1850 and Tosorontio Township in 1855; the two merged to form the Township of Adjala-Tosorontio on January 1, 1994.

Lisle is generally bounded by Main Street to the west, with its remaining edges following local streets, lot lines or natural features. It covers approximately 89 hectares.

No major adverse influences, such as hydro corridors, rail lines, highways, cemeteries, treatment plants or industrial lands, were identified within or along the edges of Lisle.

Lisle is primarily residential, with no major landmarks identified from available map data.

04.10.0010.t:
Angus, Essa

Angus began as a small settlement called Pine River, on the Nottawasaga and Pine rivers. The railway arrived in the 1850s, and the village was laid out in 1857 and named after Angus Morrison, a local politician. It was a lumbering centre until the timber ran out in the late 1800s. The village grew again with the nearby military base, now CFB Borden, and is the largest community in the Township of Essa.

Angus is generally bounded by Mill Street to the north, 5th Line to the east, Willoughby Road to the south and Barrie-Collingwood Rail Trail and Brentwood Road to the west, and covers approximately 925 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include a wastewater treatment plant and Angus Union Cemetery. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Green space in Angus includes Angus Community Park, Stonemount Park and Peacekeepers Park, and the Nottawasaga River and the Pine River run through or along the community. Residents are served by approximately 4 schools and the Angus branch of the Essa Public Library. Other notable landmarks include CFB Borden (adjacent).

08.08.0015.t:
Southgate, Southgate

Southgate is a township in Grey County, formed on January 1, 2000 by joining the Village of Dundalk with Proton and Egremont townships. The area was settled in the 1850s as farmland along the settlement roads now known as Highways 10 and 6. Dundalk, first known as McDowell's Corners, moved closer to the Toronto Grey and Bruce Railway in the 1870s and was incorporated as a village in 1887. Dundalk and Holstein are the largest communities.

Southgate is generally bounded by the Grey Highlands boundary to the north, the Melancthon boundary to the east, the East Luther Grand Valley boundary to the south and the Wellington North boundary to the west, and covers approximately 16,784 hectares.

Adverse influences within the community include a hydro transmission corridor. Properties near these influences may be affected by noise, traffic, views or market appeal, and should be considered on an individual basis.

Southgate is primarily residential, with no major landmarks identified from available map data.
